content:
The test image shows soybean leaves with a mottled light/dark green mosaic pattern, puckered/wrinkled leaf texture, and no discrete fungal lesions or spots. This strongly suggests a viral disease causing mosaic symptoms.

Top candidates: Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus.

The reference image for Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus shows seed staining symptoms. However, BPMV also causes characteristic leaf mosaic/mottling and rugosity — matching the test image well.

The test image features:
- Clear light/dark green mosaic mottling across all leaves
- Leaf puckering and rugosity (wrinkled texture)
- Systemic spread across the whole plant
- No discrete lesions, spots, or necrosis

This mosaic + leaf distortion pattern is the classic foliar expression of Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus. Other candidates (Tobacco_Streak_Virus, Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus) typically show more necrotic streaking or vein-associated browning, which is absent here.
